description_for_human: Financial statements and SEC filing evidence for US-listed companies, each figure with its source.
description_for_model: Structured financial data and SEC filing evidence for US-listed public companies. Use it for reported financial statements, metric history, comparisons between companies, and the text of SEC filings. Every value carries its reporting period and the filing it came from. A value that was not reported is null and must not be estimated.

functions.name: search_companies
functions.description: Resolve a company name or ticker to the US-listed company it refers to. Use this first when a company is named ambiguously, when only a company name is known, or before another tool when the ticker is uncertain. Returns ticker, company name, SEC CIK, sector and index membership. Returns no financial data.

functions.name: get_company_financials
functions.description: Retrieve standardized historical financial metrics for one publicly traded US company, with the SEC filing that reports each fiscal period. Use for questions about a company’s revenue, profit, margins, earnings per share, share count, cash flow, debt, cash or stock-based compensation over time. Supports annual and quarterly periods. Values are returned as filed; a metric with no reported value is null and is never estimated. Not investment advice.

functions.name: get_metric_history
functions.description: Return one financial metric as a chronological series for a single company, for example diluted weighted-average shares for the last eight quarters or annual revenue for the last five fiscal years. Every observation carries its fiscal period and the SEC filing source where one exists. Use get_company_financials instead when several metrics are needed at once.

functions.name: search_filings
functions.description: Find SEC filings for one company by form type and date range. Returns each filing’s form, filing date, reporting period, accession number, the SEC document description and a direct SEC source URL. Use this to locate a 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, proxy or other filing; use get_filing_content to read text from one of the results. This searches filing metadata, not the text inside filings.

functions.name: get_filing_content
functions.description: Retrieve relevant excerpts from one SEC filing instead of the whole document. Request a section by name (for example "Risk Factors", "MD&A" or "Legal Proceedings") or search the filing’s narrative for a term (for example "AWS", "gross margin" or "share repurchases"). Returns short excerpts with the section they came from and the filing URL. Defaults to the company’s latest 10-K; pass a form or an accession number from search_filings to choose another filing. Use this for what management said in a filing, and get_company_financials for numbers.

functions.name: compare_company_metrics
functions.description: Compare two to five publicly traded US companies on the same standardized metrics, using each company’s filed periods. Use for questions that put companies side by side, such as operating margins or revenue growth across peers. Returns one series per metric with a value per company and fiscal period, the units, and the SEC filing source for each value. Companies with different fiscal period ends are flagged and their periods are never blended.

functions.name: get_financial_change_drivers
functions.description: Return the reported arithmetic behind a change in a company’s results between two fiscal periods: revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit, operating expenses, operating income, other non-operating income, income tax, net income, and the split of an earnings-per-share change into a net-income effect and a share-count effect. Every input is a reported line item with its SEC filing source, and each bridge step’s components sum to that step’s change. This is reported arithmetic, not a causal explanation or investment advice.
